messages:
noa: quick sync: i'm proposing we migrate from the flat 'metric_envelope' schema to a small hierarchical envelope that separates route_profile + measurement_id. reason: console queries for quotas/alerts keep touching a huge JSONB field and its killing p99s.

priya: high level: what are the columns and keys?

noa: new shape: columns: tenant_id, route_profile_id, measurement_id, day, value, tags (sparsed). The big change is replacing freeform metric_envelope JSONB with structured fields so we can index measurement_id and route_profile_id independently.

jun: will old clients break? existing dashboard code reads metric_envelope -> metric.name etc.

noa: plan is adapter shim that unmarshals old API. two phases: write-side dualwrite to both schemas, then backfill, then cut reads. adapter returns an envelope-compatible structure for now.

tom: backfill strategy? i want to avoid long table locks.

noa: steps:
1) Add new columns with defaults NULL.
2) Spawn parallel worker that scans batches and populates route_profile_id & measurement_id derived from metric_envelope lookup tables.
3) Create partial indexes incrementally (concurrent where supported).
4) Switch ingesters to write both shapes.
5) Canary reads for 5% tenants via feature flag.

priya: how do you compute route_profile_id? we have many ad-hoc route tags today.

noa: well normalize: a route_profile is a canonical set of tags (product area, env, privacy_tier). we'll compute hash(profile_tags) and map to route_profile_id in a small mapping table per-tenant. existing tag collisions will be resolved by a migration util that suggests merges and flags conflicts to the owners.

jun: storage/perf notes? this will create a small mapping table and reduce JSONB reads. Should improve p99 but may increase joins during writes.

noa: yep tradeoff. write CPU will slightly increase but read indexable access should drop p99 significantly. also enables easier per-profile quotas in console.

tom: can we add a roll-forward path in case mapping table inconsistent? e.g., if mapping misses, adapter should fall back to scanning metric_envelope.

noa: good call. adapter has fallback: if route_profile_id is NULL, use envelope decode and on-the-fly mapping. but log and metric that occurs; exclude high-frequency tenants from fallback.

priYa: spelling nit :) also we need reconciliation: daily job that validates sums of measurement_id aggregates between old and new shapes for canary tenants. alert on >0.2% diff.

noa: agreed. i'll add diff thresholds and a drift dashboard.

ops-bot: migration scheduled: envelopes.hierarchical.addcols v1 -> 2026-05-10T04:00:00Z (owner: noa).

jun: DBA ops: create indexes concurrently and set low maintenance_work_mem for workers. throttle backfill with MAX_ROWS_PER_TX to avoid long GC pauses.

noa: we'll coordinate with infra to reserve a maintenance window. also changing ingestion: we'll add route_profile_id derivation into the ingest lambda in phase 1 to avoid UPDATE storms.

tom: dashboard side: console needs a new UI toggle to show "profile view" and a migration banner for customers who have ambiguous tags. UX should call out that some historical metrics are being remapped during backfill.

priYa: do we need consent for PII-sensitive tags? profile computation must remove any PII before hash. add KMS-salt per-org for hashing.

noa: already on the plan: strip PII from tags and use tenant_salt + KMS for consistent hashing. will include security review.

jun: final ask: add abort criteria: if canary p99 latency regresses >25% or reconciliation >0.5% abort and revert reads.

noa: adding both to runbook. i'll write RFC with schema DDL, backfill job, adapter contract, canary metrics and rollback steps. posting for review by EOW.

priYa: ping infra and console teams in RFC thread. :pray:

noa: will do, thanks everyone.
